Subject: Proposed maintenance window & questions about version pinning for private deployment

Hi Naomi,

We're planning our quarterly maintenance for the Acme Health VPC deployment and want to coordinate Redwood's private node patching. Our preliminary window is Friday, June 11, 00:30–03:30 PDT (low traffic). Before we lock it in we have a few questions: 

- Can Redwood support a version-lock (pin) on the control plane and inference runtime for a rolling patch so we don't advance model-serving versions automatically?
- What are the recommended TTLs for DNS and how long should we keep route-table GRACE entries during a rollback?
- If we need to abort, what is the expected RTO to restore the previous pinned config?

Would appreciate a short runbook or checklist we can attach to our change request. Attaching our maintenance calendar stub.

Thanks,
Karen Li
IT Operations Manager
Acme Health

Subject: Re: Proposed maintenance window & questions about version pinning for private deployment

Hi Karen — thanks for the heads-up. Short answers up front, details below and a draft runbook attached.

- Yes: we can pin both the private control plane agent and the model runtime image per-namespace for the duration of the window.
- Recommended DNS TTL: 30s for the LB DNS during rollout, full DNS lowerings 24 hours pre-change to reduce cached routes.
- RTO for rollback: typical target is 15–30 minutes to revert traffic routing, 60 minutes to fully restore state to pre-patch if we need rehydration of caches.

Next steps I propose:
1) Redwood to provide a short maintenance runbook and network ACL diff (attached).
2) CloudOps to confirm firewall/port rules and schedule for cert rotation if needed.
3) We run a canary on 10% of nodes for the first 30 minutes, then 50%, then full.
4) If an abort is required at any stage we flip the ALB back to the pinned backend set and rehydrate KV caches from warm snapshots.

I attached a draft runbook (upgrade-runbook-v2.pdf). Please review and we can lock the date. Lauren — can you own external comms once we confirm? Dev — see the technical questions inline.

Cheers,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Proposed maintenance window & questions about version pinning for private deployment

Hi all — adding technical clarifications from the serving/runtime side: 

- Version pinning: We support image tags and a control-plane flag that pins the runtime and kernel shim for a cluster. That prevents autosync upgrades from our control plane. The pin is namespace-scoped; we will apply it to the Acme production namespace and your canary namespace separately.

- Rolling strategy: Node drain -> container stop -> node patch -> start -> KV cache warm -> health check pass -> remove from LB. Draining each node is expected to be 60–120s of paused inference traffic (requests routed to other nodes).

- Canary plan: 10% for 30 min, if SLOs stable (latency P95 within 10% and error rate <0.5%) advance to 50% for 20 min, then 100%. We will capture token-level cost deltas and include them in post-mortem.

- Backout steps (high-level):
  1) Stop rollout and remove new nodes from LB.
  2) Re-point LB to previously pinned backend set (we keep one immutable pinned backend snapshot per patch).
  3) If control-plane requires state rollback, restore the control-plane config from the pre-patch snapshot (we take a config and KV snapshot right before the first canary step).
  4) Rehydrate caches from snapshots stored in the private S3 bucket (takes ~10–45 min depending on working set).

- Network: During the window we will ask for ephemeral lowering of DNS TTL (as Naomi suggested). For route-table grace we recommend keeping a 15-minute BGP/route stability window, and hold ACLs stable until post-validation. CloudOps: confirm ability to flip route table entries within 5 minutes.

Attachments: I included a quick network ACL diff and the exact sysctl/kernel/prepatch checklist (network-acl-diff.xlsx). Note: if there's a GPU driver update required on the nodes, rollback requires reinstalling previous driver + container runtime restart — add ~30–45 min.

Happy to run a dry-run in our staging VPC next week.

— Dev
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: network-acl-diff.xlsx (xls)]
